correctness.rationale: Reconstructed definitions and both inequalities for all n>=3. Zero-coordinate windows enforce two distinct host ones per disjoint block; for any e=z-(n-2), t>=2ceil((n-1)/(e+1)). AM–GM gives lower bound. Explicit grid host W_g with g=ceil(sqrt((n-2)/2)) selects a valid pair for every nonnegative a,b,c, with j<=m and enough zeros after the second one. Rounding gives claimed upper bound. Python exact enumeration through n=11 and all-target grid checks through n=160 replay successfully; these checks are supplemental not used as infinite proof. No outside certificate or independent validation claimed.

originality.rationale: published-finding corpus semantic searches using the exact fixed-weight-two source family, Parikh-composition aliases, sparse subsequences and the square-root coefficient returned only different quantified problems. Full accessible primary texts were inspected: Clifford et al. (2010) address resource-constrained coverage; Uznański (2015) distinct-symbol permutations; Ma (2025) balanced fixed-content targets; published binary-universality and insertion-radius results address all targets, rather than the sparse layer. None of those statements, their stated stronger implications, or their proofs yields the sharp sqrt overhead claimed here. Residual risk of unindexed or overlooked stronger work is explicitly retained.
residual_risks: An unindexed or differently named treatment of universal supersequences of multiset permutations (two copies of one letter) may already obtain the coefficient.
Ma's broader rearrangement machinery might permit a derivation not explicitly stated as a theorem; no decisive stronger implication was identified in inspected text.
published-finding corpus is a semantic index and ranked search cannot prove global uniqueness. Independent audit has not been performed.

value.rationale: Determines previously unestablished (in inspected literature) sharp square-root overhead coefficient for a natural fixed-composition family of binary strings, contrasting the linear overhead required for unrestricted binary universality and balanced targets. The lower packing obstruction and matching uniformly spaced host construction explain the structural source of the coefficient. It is a nontrivial asymptotic characterization, not a cosmetic variant, one-off numerical result, or a textbook normalization check.
